statement.p: A fence is to be built to enclose a rectangular area of 290 square feet. The fence along three sides is to be made of material that costs 6 dollars per foot, and the material for the fourth side costs 14 dollars per foot. Find the dimensions of the enclosure that is most economical to construct.

solution.p: A rectangle has sides x and y. Since the names of the variables don't matter, say one of the y sides costs 14 dollars per foot and the other one and the two sides of length x all cost 6 dollars per square foot. Then the total cost of the fencing is C=6 x + 6 x + 6 y + 14 y= 12 x + 20 y We are trying to minimize this function, but we need to reduce it to one variable. However, we are also given that the area of this rectangle is 290. Thus, xy=290, and solving for one of the variables, y=\frac{290}{x}.

Substituting back into the cost function, we get C= 12 x+ 20 \left(\frac{290}{x} \right) = 12 x+ 5800 x^{-1} Take the derivative and set it equal to 0. C'=12 - 5800 x^{-2}= 12 + \frac{-5800}{x^2}=0 Multiply both sides by x^2 12 x^2-5800=0 and solve x=\sqrt{\frac{5800}{12}}=21.9848432637882 \mbox{ ft.} (Why didn't I know that it wasn't x=-\sqrt{\frac{5800}{12}}=-21.9848432637882 ? )
